cards.title: Sixteen, in Lucknow, building a health app
cards.body: Vyom Ahuja is 16 and building AICA from Lucknow. Here are a few lessons from the early days, kept honest and simple.

cards.title: Start with a real, boring problem
cards.body: Lost prescriptions, missed doses, confusing handwriting. Not flashy problems, but ones families deal with every week. That's where AICA started.

cards.title: Build for how India actually prescribes
cards.body: 1-0-1, half tablets, a chemist uncle who knows the family. An app built for somewhere else wouldn't fit. The details have to be local.

cards.title: AI helps, people decide
cards.body: Reading prescriptions with AI is useful, but mistakes in health matter. So every scan gets checked by a person before it's saved.

cards.title: Trust has to be designed in
cards.body: Consent at sign-up, data never sold, download or delete anytime. Decided early, not bolted on later.

cards.title: Show something before promising everything
cards.body: An interactive prototype says more than a pitch. AICA started there, with a waitlist, well before any app store listing.

cards.title: Still early, still learning
cards.body: Pilots are starting in Lucknow. To follow along or help shape it, the prototype and waitlist are at aicaglobal.in.

takeaway: Pick a real problem, build for Indian prescriptions, keep people in the loop and design trust in early.
share: A 16-year-old in Lucknow is building AICA, a health app for Indian families. aicaglobal.in
